concepts.def: Repeated cycle of designing, prototyping and testing that progressively refines a product based on feedback.
Initial statement of the problem and requirements set by a client or identified through research, initiating the design process.
Set of measurable criteria a product must meet, covering function, materials, dimensions, cost and user needs.
Working or appearance model of a design used to test ideas, gather user feedback and refine specifications.
Critical review of a prototype against the specification, identifying improvements for the next iteration.
Information gathered from intended users through interviews, observation or testing, feeding decisions for iteration.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Processes & Manufacture — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Processes & Manufacture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Processes & Manufacture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which document sets out measurable criteria a product must meet?
options: Brief
Specification
Catalogue
Bill of materials
Single linear process
Repeated cycles of refinement
No prototyping
Fixed first solution

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: It stays constant.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
They are the same thing with different names.

mcqs.q: Why can thermoplastics be recycled but thermosets cannot?
options: Thermosets are too dangerous to recycle.
Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be remoulded; thermosets have cross-links that lock the shape permanently.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Thermoplastics are cheaper, so it is worth recycling them.

mcqs.q: What does an LDR's resistance do as light intensity INCREASES?
options: It decreases.
It stays constant.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
It increases (more light = more resistance).
